hypothesis: Unconsumed response streams can affect Wrangler test-harness connection lifetime.
change: Test-only fetchComplete drains each actual Worker response via arrayBuffer before issuing the next request and reconstructs a response with identical status, statusText, headers and body for all existing assertions. No retry, application error conversion or production change.

comparison.original: Multiple isolated serial runs reproduced network-category non-JSON 500; ten intervening runs passed.
comparison.explicitConsumption: 20 consecutive fresh Worker runs passed; full admin suite 188 passed, zero failures/skips.
comparison.conclusion: Evidence supports response lifecycle involvement; finite successful runs do not establish the exact runtime root cause or guarantee CI stability.

diagnostics: Unexpected 500 reports request ordinal and count of fully consumed preceding responses. No body, token, secret, URL or identifier is printed.
processObservation: Public Wrangler TestHarness API exposes no child PID/exit callback. An OS read of own diagnostic process tree confirmed test Node existence at inspection, but was not contemporaneous with a 500 and does not establish workerd liveness at failure.
remaining: Confirm on Linux CI. If failure recurs, preceding-response count rules out incomplete client-side response consumption; obtain fixed runtime event classification without raw log publication.
